subject.title: fix(infra): reject oversized gateway TLS files before reading

question: What permanent size and filesystem-safety contract should gateway TLS certificate, key, and CA inputs enforce without breaking existing CA-bundle configurations?
rationale: The patch creates a new fail-closed upgrade boundary and security contract; choosing one universal limit versus role-specific limits cannot be resolved safely from tests alone.

options.title: Shared reader with role-specific caps
options.body: Use the established fs-safe read boundary, retain a tight certificate/key limit, and give CA bundles a separately justified and documented maximum with upgrade coverage.

options.title: Keep one 256 KiB cap
options.body: Accept that some existing TLS configurations may stop starting, and explicitly document and prove that compatibility decision before merge.

options.title: Defer the hard limit
options.body: Close or pause this PR until a repository-wide TLS-file policy and migration-safe limits are defined.

recommendation.title: Shared reader with role-specific caps
recommendation.body: Use the established fs-safe read boundary, retain a tight certificate/key limit, and give CA bundles a separately justified and documented maximum with upgrade coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The most relevant available history is the recent work maintaining OpenClaw's fail-closed fs-safe secret-file contract.
